asthma_respiratory.title: Pediatric Asthma & Viral Chest Infection Screener

questions.label: Frequent, recurring dry cough, especially at night or early morning
Audible whistling or wheezing sound when breathing out
Visible chest indrawing (skin sucking in around ribs/neck during breaths)
History of rapid breathing or shortness of breath with physical activity

recommendations.Low: Normal respiratory indicators. Monitor for seasonal viral triggers.
recommendations.Moderate: Moderate risk of pediatric airway hyper-reactivity or viral bronchiolitis. Keep rescue protocols ready and consult a clinician.
recommendations.High: High risk of acute respiratory distress / asthma exacerbation. Urgent clinical evaluation required immediately.

questions.label: Persistent cough lasting more than 2 weeks
Unexplained weight loss, failure to thrive, or lack of appetite
Drenching night sweats or recurring afternoon/evening fevers
Known close household contact with an active TB patient

recommendations.Low: Low clinical index for active TB. Continue standard wellness tracking.
recommendations.Moderate: Moderate TB risk indicators present. Schedule a sputum smear or GeneXpert test at the local clinic.
recommendations.High: High probability score for Tuberculosis. Immediate clinical isolation, chest X-ray, and evaluation required.

questions.label: Maternal history of positive HIV status during pregnancy or breastfeeding
Recurrent severe infections, persistent diarrhea, or chronic oral thrush
Severe slow growth or developmental milestone delays in infants

recommendations.Low: No primary exposure indicators noted. Maintain standard routine immunizations.
recommendations.Moderate: Moderate risk markers identified. Counsel for voluntary HIV counseling and testing (VCT) or infant PCR follow-up.
recommendations.High: High risk score for pediatric/adult HIV indicator conditions. Prioritize urgent clinical testing and ART referral.
